options.text: Make sure top management is committed and knows what will be required.
Begin by trying to reduce setup times while maintaining the current system.
Gradually convert operations, beginning at the end of the process and working backward.
As one of the first steps, convert suppliers to JIT.
Cut inventories first in order to expose problems, before major problems have been resolved.
Obtain the support and cooperation of workers, including reassuring them that their jobs are secure.

questions.stem: Which of the following is (are) *incorrect* regarding obstacles to conversion to a lean system?

options.text: Management that is not totally committed or unwilling to devote resources is perhaps the most serious impediment.
Managers may resist because lean shifts responsibility from management to workers.
Workers may resist because lean reduces their responsibility.
Suppliers may resist because the burden of quality control shifts to the supplier.
Suppliers may be uneasy about long-term commitments.
Managers may resist because lean gives them more control over workers.
